question.problem:
What is the missing part of the expression below?

$$
-\frac{11}{9}=\frac{\bbox[1pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}{9}
$$
question.worked_solution:
A negative number can be obtained if we divide two numbers, one of which is positive and the other negative.

So, given a negative fraction, we have the following equivalent notations:

$$
-\frac{11}{9}=\frac{-11}{9}=\frac{11}{-9}
$$

In our case, we see that the denominator on the right-hand side is positive $(9).$ Therefore, the missing numerator must be $(-11):$

$$
-\frac{11}{9}=\frac{-11}{9}
$$
